The "transition generation" generally refers to individuals born in the early years of a country's pension reform, often those affected by the shift from a defined benefit to a defined contribution pension system. The exact age group can vary by country and the specific reform timeline.

Regarding the impact of early payment of the AHV (Alters- und Hinterlassenenversicherung, Swiss Old-Age and Survivors' Insurance) pension: In Switzerland, early retirement is possible, but it results in a reduction of the pension amount. The earlier you retire, the lower your pension will be compared to retiring at the full retirement age. The reduction is typically a percentage of the full pension amount for each year you retire before the full retirement age.
